label: Caused intellect: an intellect whose being some other being causes
term: created intellect, weakest typed reading (intellectus creatus; Lean `IsCausedIntellect`)
definition: IsCausedIntellect CausesIn esse HasIntellect x: x has intellect (HAS_INTELLECT_1) and some being c other than x causes x's being (CausesIn c x esse). The typed reading of 'created intellect' in ST I q.12 a.7. Example: on the stage-two route, any other intellectual being, whose being the being with the nine causes (IsCreatorOfAll). Counterexample: a being with intellect whose being nothing other than it causes. Weaker than created in the Dei Filius sense: creation from no presupposed subject, freedom and a beginning are not encoded (as in IsCreatorOfAll, definition 92c03350).
note: Analyst reading, attribution deferred. Used in INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2 (definition 94ebe0d2). Structural properties: none built in. SCOPE CONDITION (an explicit domain stipulation, binding every premise that shares this Being and CausesIn, including 'Whatever has its being caused by another is not INFINITE_1'): elements of Being are individuated by their act of being, so things numerically one in esse are one element. The divine persons share one numerically identical esse, so they are not distinct elements and cannot be represented as such in this vocabulary; the Son's being from the Father is no instance of CausesIn c x esse with c distinct from x. That q.33 a.1 ad 1 prefers 'principle' to 'cause' is only a terminological aside (the reply notes that the Greeks use 'cause'); the scope condition does not rest on it.
